claims.text: Annealing at an optimized temperature followed by controlled rapid cooling will refine eutectic lamellar spacing relative to the as-cast state.
Refining the eutectic lamellar spacing through this treatment will simultaneously increase strength and ductility.
The initial as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy has a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure.
The treatment consists of an annealing hold for a predetermined time followed by controlled rapid cooling.
The proposed improvement should occur during ambient-temperature mechanical testing.
The proposed treatment is applicable under normal atmospheric processing conditions.
The treatment will produce reduced and more uniform eutectic lamellar spacing.
Reduced and more uniform lamellar spacing enhances dislocation-barrier effects.
Reduced and more uniform lamellar spacing improves phase connectivity.
The refined lamellar microstructure increases strength by impeding dislocation motion.
The refined lamellar microstructure promotes distributed plastic deformation.
The treatment should increase yield strength by approximately 20% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treatment should maintain or slightly enhance ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
The as-cast baseline exhibits high tensile ductility and high fracture strength.
The beneficial response exists only within a specific thermal-processing window.
Processing outside the beneficial window may cause undesired phase transformations or over-coarsening that negate the mechanical benefits.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in both yield strength and ductility, or improvement of one at the expense of the other, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis promises an increase in both strength and ductility, whereas the predicted outcome permits ductility merely to be maintained. The falsification rule then requires statistically significant improvements in both properties, so an outcome allowed by the prediction would nevertheless falsify the stated hypothesis.
